name: dsi_pll_28nm_clk_recalc_rate
prose: Static unsigned long (dsi_phy_28nm.c:242-288) that returns the VCO rate in Hz computed from the PLL registers; the parent_rate argument is only logged and is not used in the result. It starts with ref_clk = VCO_REF_CLK_RATE and adds VCO_REF_CLK_RATE times the masked DBLR bit of REFCLK_CFG (so the reference is doubled when the doubler bit is set). It reads SDM_CFG0: if its bypass bit is set it returns ref_clk times (the BYP_DIV field plus 1); otherwise it reads the DC_OFFSET field of SDM_CFG1 and the frequency seed built from the FREQ_SEED_15_8 field of SDM_CFG3 (high byte) and FREQ_SEED_7_0 field of SDM_CFG2 (low byte), and returns ref_clk * (dc_offset + 1) + mult_frac(ref_clk, seed, 65536). It reads registers only and takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head: the function is dsi_pll_28nm_clk_recalc_rate (head at dsi_phy_28nm.c:242). The old prose said ref_clk is parent_rate plus VCO_REF_CLK_RATE, which is wrong: ref_clk starts from the constant VCO_REF_CLK_RATE (249) and parent_rate is not used (only logged at 252). R:n/a

name: msm_atomic_commit_tail
prose: Void function (msm_atomic.c:213-324). It computes the CRTC mask and whether the update can use the async path (single CRTC), calls kms->funcs->enable_commit, locks the CRTCs, waits for the previous flush (wait_flush), clears the fault snapshot flag, calls prepare_commit if present, and pushes the update with drm_atomic_helper_commit_modeset_disables, commit_planes and commit_modeset_enables. In the async case it warns if the mask is not the single async CRTC; if no update is already pending for that CRTC it sets the pending bit and computes the next vblank start, goes to the fallback path when that fails, and otherwise queues the timer work one millisecond before it; then it calls disable_commit, unlocks the CRTCs, calls commit_hw_done and cleanup_planes and returns, with the pending bit left set and without flush_commit, a second wait_flush or complete_commit. In the fallback (non-async or failed async) path it clears the CRTC bits from pending_crtc_mask, takes vblank references, calls flush_commit, unlocks, waits for the flush, drops the vblank references, locks again, calls complete_commit, unlocks, calls disable_commit, then commit_hw_done and cleanup_planes. It returns nothing.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at msm_atomic.c:213). Reviewer claim (the async fast path skips flush_commit, wait_flush and complete_commit, contradicting the old 'always' postcondition) is right: 251-288. R:right

name: msm_fbdev_driver_fbdev_probe
prose: Returns int (msm_fbdev.c:91-157). It computes the DRM format from the surface bpp and depth, aligns the pitch and allocates a stolen framebuffer with msm_alloc_stolen_fb; if that returns an error pointer it logs and returns PTR_ERR(fb) directly, without calling drm_framebuffer_remove (nothing was allocated to remove). Otherwise it gets the first plane's GEM object, pins it in priv->kms->vm with msm_gem_get_and_pin_iova (on error it goes to fail), sets helper->funcs and helper->fb, sets fbi->fbops, fills the fb_info with drm_fb_helper_fill_info, and maps the object with msm_gem_get_vaddr into fbi->screen_buffer (on an error pointer it goes to fail). On success it sets fbi->screen_size, fix.smem_start (the iova) and fix.smem_len and returns 0. At fail it calls drm_framebuffer_remove(fb) and returns the error; in the case where msm_gem_get_vaddr failed, helper->fb still points to the framebuffer that was removed.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at msm_fbdev.c:91). Reviewer claim (the allocation failure returns PTR_ERR(fb) without calling drm_framebuffer_remove, contrary to the old prose) is right (113-116). R:right

name: msm_ioctl_vm_bind
prose: Returns int (msm_gem_vma.c:1411-1611). It takes the queue lock itself (the caller must not hold it). It returns -ENXIO if there is no GPU, -EPIPE if the VM is unusable, -EINVAL for a context without vmbind support or invalid flags, and -ENOENT if the submit queue is not found. After that, errors go through cleanup: -EINVAL for a queue that is not a VM_BIND queue; the error from get_unused_fd_flags (when MSM_VM_BIND_FENCE_FD_OUT is set); vm_bind_job_create; mutex_lock_interruptible on queue->lock; an invalid in-fence (-EINVAL) or the error from adding it as a dependency; parse errors for in and out syncobjs; vm_bind_job_lookup_ops; vm_bind_prealloc_count; and within a drm_exec section, lock, pin and prepare of the job's objects; and -ENOMEM if sync_file_create fails. On success it arms the job and takes a fence reference, attaches fences, pushes the job to the scheduler, resets the input syncobjs, processes the output post deps with the fence and returns 0 after installing the out-fence fd and writing it to args->fence_fd. On failure paths it unpins the objects (if past the pin step), finalises the exec, unlocks the queue, releases the unused fd and any sync_file, frees the job, and in every case (success or failure) it drops the post_deps and syncobjs_to_reset arrays and their references; msm_submitqueue_put is called only when the job is NULL or an error pointer.
note: slice cut the head: the function is msm_ioctl_vm_bind (head at msm_gem_vma.c:1411); there is no msm_vm_bind_ioctl_submit_path. The old prose assumed the caller holds queue->lock; this function takes and releases it (1472, 1571). R:n/a

name: nv04_display_create
prose: Returns int (dispnv04/disp.c:211-307). It allocates the nv04_display with vzalloc and returns -ENOMEM on failure; otherwise it stores it in nouveau_display(dev)->priv with the dtor, init and fini callbacks, clears DRIVER_ATOMIC, and, when the DRM device has a channel, constructs the 'kmsFlip' event (a failure returns that error with the display left installed in nouveau_display(dev)->priv). It saves the VGA fonts, creates one CRTC (two when the chip has two heads), and for each DCB entry creates a connector (an error pointer skips the entry) and then the DAC, DFP, or TV output for the entry's type; failed creations and unknown types are skipped (the latter with a warning) and do not fail the function. It destroys any connector with no possible encoders, assigns each encoder's i2c bus from the DCB i2c index (NULL if none found), saves the state of every CRTC and encoder, calls nouveau_overlay_init and returns 0.
note: slice cut the head: the function is nv04_display_create (head at dispnv04/disp.c:211); the old prose omitted the -ENOMEM and the event-constructor error returns. R:n/a

name: nv50_wndw_atomic_check
prose: Static int (dispnv50/wndw.c:442-521). If the new plane state has a CRTC it gets the head atom (returning PTR_ERR on failure, before asyw->visible has been assigned), records whether a modeset is needed, and sets asyw->visible to the head's active state; with no CRTC visible is false. If the old state had a CRTC it gets that head atom (PTR_ERR on failure). If the window is visible, has an xlut_set hook and the old state was not visible or the colour management or format changed, it calls nv50_wndw_atomic_check_lut (error returned). If visible it calls nv50_wndw_atomic_check_acquire (error returned, after asyw fields may already be modified) and sets the window's bit in asyh->wndw.mask; else if it was previously visible it calls nv50_wndw_atomic_check_release and clears the bit in the old head's mask; else it returns 0 immediately. When the window is not visible or a modeset is needed it sets clr.ntfy, clr.sema, clr.xlut and clr.csc from whether the old state had those handles or valid CSC (set.xlut is set again when the window stays visible and has an xlut handle), and sets clr.image from the old image handle only if wndw->func->image_clr exists. It then returns 0.
note: Checked against wndw.c:442-521. Reviewer claims: acquire failure leaves asyw modified (right, 491-494), visible is not updated before the PTR_ERR return for the new CRTC (right, 462-466), clr.image is set only when the image_clr hook exists (right, 516-517). R:right

name: nouveau_gem_ioctl_pushbuf
prose: Returns int (nouveau_gem.c:754-988). It returns -ENOMEM if nouveau_abi16_get fails; after that every return goes through nouveau_abi16_put(abi16, ret). It returns -ENOSYS if the client uses UVMM, -ENOENT if no ABI16 channel matches req->channel, -ENODEV if that channel is killed. It records the SYNC flag from req->vram_available and overwrites the field with the available VRAM, sets gart_available, and if req->nr_push is 0 it skips the whole submission (no pushes queued and no fence created) and returns 0 after setting the suffix words. Otherwise it returns -EINVAL if nr_push, nr_buffers or nr_relocs exceed the maximums, copies the push, buffer and reloc arrays from user space (PTR_ERR of a failed u_memcpya), returns -EINVAL if a push's bo_index is not below nr_buffers, validates the buffers (error returned; relocations are copied and the validation redone when needed), applies relocations (error), waits for ring space and queues the pushes in one of three ways by channel class and chipset (errors from nvif_chan_gpfifo_wait, PUSH_WAIT or ttm_bo_kmap returned), creates a fence (error returned), and when SYNC was requested waits for it (the fence status 1 becomes 0). At the end it releases the validation state and fence and, when relocations were done, copies back to user space the buffers' presumed fields that are not valid (a copy_to_user failure sets -EFAULT, even if the submission itself succeeded). It frees the copies and sets the suffix words by channel class before returning.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at nouveau_gem.c:754). Reviewer claim (the old prose omitted the nr_push == 0 success path that queues nothing) is right (794-795). R:right

name: nvkm_firmware_ctor
prose: Returns int (nvkm/core/firmware.c:225-309). It stores func, name, device and len in fw and switches on fw->func->type. For NVKM_FIRMWARE_IMG_RAM it kmemdups the image. For NVKM_FIRMWARE_IMG_DMA it allocates a page-aligned noncoherent DMA buffer, copies the data and records the DMA address, and initialises the single scatterlist with sg_init_one even if the allocation failed. For NVKM_FIRMWARE_IMG_SGT it vmallocs a page-aligned buffer, copies the data, allocates an sg table, fills it with the pages from vmalloc_to_page (a NULL page gives -EFAULT) and maps it for DMA_TO_DEVICE; if any of that fails it frees the table, vfree's the image and sets fw->img to NULL. Any other type executes WARN_ON(1) and returns -EINVAL. After the switch it returns -ENOMEM if fw->img is NULL (so every failure above, including the -EFAULT case, is reported as -ENOMEM); otherwise it constructs the memory object with nvkm_memory_ctor and returns 0.

name: nvkm_mm_init
prose: Returns int (nvkm/core/mm.c:239-280) and adds a heap region [offset, offset+length) to the allocator. If the mm is already initialised it takes the end of the last node; if that differs from offset it BUG_ONs when it is above offset and otherwise allocates (kzalloc, -ENOMEM on failure) a HOLE node for the gap and appends it to mm->nodes; it also BUG_ONs when block differs from mm->block_size. If the mm was not initialised it initialises the node and free lists, sets block_size and zeroes heap_nodes. It then allocates a node (kzalloc; -ENOMEM on failure, in which case the hole node added above stays in the list), and when length is nonzero sets node->offset to the block-rounded-up offset and node->length to the block-rounded-down end minus that offset; with length 0 the node has zero offset and length. It appends the node to mm->nodes and mm->free, sets node->heap to heap, increments mm->heap_nodes and returns 0. nvkm_mm_fini frees the nodes.
note: slice cut the head: the function is nvkm_mm_init (head at mm.c:239), which also handles an already-initialised mm and adds a hole node; the old prose said mm is unchanged on failure, which is false after a hole node was added. R:n/a

name: nvkm_device_ctor
prose: Returns int (nvkm/engine/device/base.c:3140-3461). It takes nv_devices_mutex for the whole call and returns -EEXIST if a device with the same handle is already listed. It fills in func, quirk, dev, type, handle and options, adds the device to nv_devices (it stays there on failure), maps BAR0 into device->pri (-ENOMEM if that fails), and switches the GPU to the CPU's endianness (-ENOSYS if that fails). It reads BOOT0 (replaced by a derived value when the NvChipset option is set), derives chipset, chiprev and card_type, selects the chip description from the chipset number, and returns -ENODEV for an unknown chipset unless the unsupported-chipsets option selects chipset 0x170. It returns -ENODEV for card types from TU100 on when BOOT1 indicates a vGPU. It reads the strap register to set the crystal frequency, sets the name, initialises the mutex and interrupt state, and constructs each subdev and engine listed in the chip layout: a constructor error other than -ENODEV logs and returns that error; an -ENODEV is swallowed (the subdev is deleted and its pointer cleared) and construction continues. The final result is that of nvkm_intr_install, which overwrites a swallowed -ENODEV. On any nonzero result, if device->pri is set it is unmapped and cleared. The mutex is released at done.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at base.c:3140; the call takes nine arguments). Reviewer claim (a subdevice constructor's -ENODEV is swallowed and not returned) is right (3418-3425, 3453). R:right

name: nvkm_disp_new_
prose: Returns int (nvkm/engine/disp/base.c:228-262) and creates the display engine. It allocates *pdisp with kzalloc (-ENOMEM on failure, leaving *pdisp NULL), stores func and initialises the heads, iors, outps and conns lists and the client lock, and constructs the engine with nvkm_engine_ctor; on an error it sets disp->func to NULL and returns the error. If func->super is set it creates a single-thread workqueue named nvkm-disp (-ENOMEM if that fails, with nothing undone), then initialises the super work with func->super and the super mutex. It returns the result of nvkm_event_init for the uevent. The work item, workqueue and mutex are initialised only when func->super is non-NULL.

name: gf117_grctx_generate_attrib
prose: Void function (ctxgf117.c:243-275) that fills the attribute and alpha circular buffer entries in a channel's context patch list. It reads the alpha and beta numbers from the chip's grctx functions, patches register 0x405830 with (beta << 16) | alpha and 0x4064c4 with ((alpha / 4) << 16) | 0xffff, then for each GPC and each PPC (up to the chip's ppc_nr) it skips PPCs not set in gr->ppc_mask[gpc]; for the others it patches the unit's 0xc0 register with the timeslice mode (1), beta times the PPC's TPC count and the running offset bo, advances bo by attrib_nr_max times the PPC's TPC count, patches the 0xe4 register with alpha times the TPC count and the running offset ao, and advances ao by alpha_nr_max times the TPC count. bo starts at 0 and ao at attrib_nr_max times the total TPC count. The writes go to the patch list through gf100_grctx_patch_wr32 and the function returns nothing.
note: slice cut the head: the function is gf117_grctx_generate_attrib (head at ctxgf117.c:243); the old prose omitted the two writes before the loop and the PPC mask test is by ppc_mask[gpc]. R:n/a

name: nvbios_pll_parse
prose: Returns int (nvkm/subdev/bios/pll.c:229-440). If type is above PLL_MAX it treats it as a register and maps it with pll_map_reg, otherwise it maps it with pll_map_type; it returns -ENOENT if a nonzero table version was found but no data offset. It then zeroes *info and sets info->type and info->reg itself (the caller does not preset reg). By table version it reads the limits: version 0x00 reads nothing; 0x10 and 0x11 read 32-bit vco frequency limits and set fixed n, m and p limits that depend on the chip; 0x20 and 0x21 read 16-bit values times 1000 and byte fields, and refclk only when len > 0x22; 0x30 and 0x40 and 0x50 follow indirect or direct layouts with their own field sets (0x40 and 0x50 set refclk; 0x40 and 0x50 also set min_p). Any other version logs an error and returns -EINVAL with info partially cleared. If refclk is still 0 it uses the device crystal, except on chip 0x51 for registers 0x680508 (with bit 0x20 of 0x680524) and 0x680520 (with bit 0x80), where it becomes 200000 or 25000 according to VGA register 0x27. If vco1.max_freq is still 0 it fills the vco1 limits from the BMP table (fixed 128000 and 256000 when the BMP version is below 0x0506), with min_m and max_m chosen by chip and crystal and max_p of 4 or 5, and sets max_p_usable. It returns 0.
note: slice cut the head: the function is nvbios_pll_parse(bios, type, info) (head at pll.c:229), there is no pll_limits_parse with ver/data/len parameters; the old prose described the later part. R:n/a

name: nvkm_hwsq_wr32
prose: Void function (nvkm/subdev/bus/hwsq.c:90-113) that appends the commands for a register write to the hwsq command buffer through hwsq_cmd, which memcpy's into hwsq->c.data at hwsq->c.size and advances the size without any bounds check. If data differs from the cached hwsq->data it appends a data command: 5 bytes with opcode 0xe2 when the upper 16 bits of data differ from the cached value, otherwise 3 bytes with opcode 0x42. It then always appends an address command, whether or not the address changed: 5 bytes with opcode 0xe0 when the upper 16 bits of addr differ from the cached hwsq->addr, otherwise 3 bytes with opcode 0x40. It finally stores addr and data in hwsq->addr and hwsq->data. It can append up to 10 bytes, so the buffer must have at least 10 bytes of free space.
note: Checked against hwsq.c:36-41 and 90-113. Reviewer claims: the address command is always emitted (right, 104-109) and the buffer needs at least 10 bytes free, not at most (right, hwsq_cmd has no bounds check). R:right

name: gk104_ram_new_
prose: Returns int (nvkm/subdev/fb/ramgk104.c:1520-1697). It allocates the gk104_ram itself with kzalloc (-ENOMEM on failure) and stores it in *pram right away, so on every later error the partially built object is reachable through *pram. It runs gf100_ram_ctor (error returned), initialises the cfg list, reads the partition count and mask from 0x022438 and 0x022554 and computes pnuts from differing partition configurations, parses all ramcfg data entries with gk104_ram_ctor_data until it returns -ENOENT (any other error is logged and returned), parses the mclk reference PLL (type 0x0c) and memory PLL (type 0x04) with nvbios_pll_parse (errors returned), looks up the two optional GPIO functions (a failed lookup is ignored, leaving those fuc registers unset), fills in the ramfuc register table (with the mode register set depending on whether the RAM is GDDR5 or DDR3), and returns 0.

name: gt215_ram_prog
prose: Static int (ramgt215.c:882-905) that executes the prepared reclock script. It reads the NvMemExec boolean option (default true). When true it sets bit 1 of register 0x001534 (mask 0x2), calls ram_exec(fuc, true), then clears bit 0 of 0x002504, clears bit 1 of 0x001534, and sets bit 4 of 0x616308 and 0x616b08. When false it only calls ram_exec(fuc, false). It always returns 0.

name: g94_i2c_aux_init
prose: Static int (auxg94.c:39-73) that arms the AUX channel for a transfer. It polls register 0x00e4e4 + ch*0x50 with 1 us delays for about 1000 iterations until the bits 0x03010000 are clear, and returns -EBUSY (writing nothing) if they never clear. It then writes 0x00100000 into the 0x00300000 field of that register and polls, again about 1000 times, for bits 0x03000000 to equal 0x01000000; on timeout it calls g94_i2c_aux_fini (clears bits 0x00310000) and returns -EBUSY. Otherwise it returns 0, leaving the programmed state in place.
note: Checked against auxg94.c:32-73. Prior prose consistent with the code; only the poll count is stated as about 1000 here since the timeout decrement runs one extra iteration. R:n/a

name: g94_i2c_aux_xfer
prose: Returns int (auxg94.c:75-165) and performs one AUX transaction on channel aux->ch. It first calls g94_i2c_aux_init; if that fails (negative result) it goes straight to out, returning that error. It reads status register 0x00e4e8+base and returns -ENXIO (at out) if bit 0x10000000 is clear. It then disables auto-DPCD, and for an even type (a write) copies *size bytes from data into a 16-byte buffer and writes it to the data registers. It builds the control word (type, length or 0x100 for a zero size), writes the address, then loops: it pulses the start sequence (with a 400 us delay when retrying), starts the transaction and polls up to about 2000 times for the busy bit to clear (a timeout sets -EIO and jumps to out_err, skipping the data read), reads the status and sets ret to 1 for reply codes 0x8 or 0x2, to -ETIMEDOUT when bit 0x100 is set and to -EIO when any of bits 0xe00 is set; it repeats while ret is nonzero, retry is true and fewer than 33 attempts were made. For an odd type (a read) it reads 16 bytes from the reply registers and copies *size bytes to data, also when the final ret is nonzero. At out_err it re-enables auto-DPCD; at out it calls g94_i2c_aux_fini. It returns ret if negative, otherwise (status & 0x000f0000) >> 16 from the last status read, which is a value from 0 to 15 (a negative return comes from init (-EBUSY), no sink (-ENXIO), timeout or error status (-EIO) or -ETIMEDOUT). The data buffer must hold 16 bytes for reads.
note: Checked against auxg94.c:75-165. Prior prose consistent with the code; added that -EBUSY comes from g94_i2c_aux_init, that auto-DPCD is only toggled after the sink check, and that the data read happens also for a nonzero final ret. R:n/a

name: nvkm_mxm_new_
prose: Returns int (nvkm/subdev/mxm/base.c:232-279). It allocates the nvkm_mxm with kzalloc and stores the pointer in *pmxm (-ENOMEM on failure, with *pmxm NULL), and constructs the subdev. It looks up the MXM table in the VBIOS; if there is none or its version byte is 0 it logs and returns 0 with mxm->mxms left NULL. Otherwise it logs the BIOS version and flags and calls mxm_shadow to locate a valid SIS (trying ROM, then DSM and WMI when configured); if none is valid it logs a warning and still returns 0. When a valid SIS is found it logs its version, walks the SIS structures with mxms_foreach, sets MXM_SANITISE_DCB in mxm->action if the NvMXMDCB option is true (default true), and returns 0. There is no -ENODEV return: a missing BIOS is not tested here.

name: PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER(__name, __reg_prefix, __handler)
prose: Raw interrupt handler generated by the PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER macro as panthor_<name>_irq_raw_handler(irq, data), where data is the struct panthor_irq. It returns IRQ_NONE if pirq->suspended is set, without touching the hardware. Otherwise it reads the <prefix>_INT_STAT register (so the hardware is read in this case) and returns IRQ_NONE if the value is zero; if it is nonzero it writes 0 to <prefix>_INT_MASK and returns IRQ_WAKE_THREAD.
note: the item named panthor_<name>_irq_raw_handler; this is the function generated by the macro at panthor_device.h:388-401. Reviewer claim (the handler must read INT_STAT even when it reads zero) is right: the old wording implied no hardware access when INT_STAT was zero. R:right

name: PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER(__name, __reg_prefix, __handler)
prose: Threaded interrupt handler generated by the PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER macro as panthor_<name>_irq_threaded_handler(irq, data). It loops reading <prefix>_INT_RAWSTAT masked with pirq->mask; for each nonzero value it calls the user handler (ptdev, status) and records IRQ_HANDLED, and stops when the masked status is zero. After the loop it writes pirq->mask back to <prefix>_INT_MASK unless pirq->suspended is set, and returns IRQ_HANDLED if at least one status was handled, otherwise IRQ_NONE.
note: item named panthor_<name>_irq_threaded_handler; generated at panthor_device.h:403-423. Reviewer claim about INT_STAT reading applies to the raw handler only. R:n/a

name: PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER(__name, __reg_prefix, __handler)
prose: Inline function generated by the PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER macro as panthor_<name>_irq_suspend(pirq). It sets pirq->mask to 0, writes 0 to <prefix>_INT_MASK, calls synchronize_irq(pirq->irq) to wait for a running handler, and then sets pirq->suspended to true. It returns nothing.
note: item named panthor_<name>_irq_suspend; generated at panthor_device.h:425-431. The round 15 reviewer claim about INT_STAT is not applicable to this function. R:n/a

name: PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER(__name, __reg_prefix, __handler)
prose: Inline function generated by the PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER macro as panthor_<name>_irq_resume(pirq, mask). It clears pirq->suspended, stores mask in pirq->mask, writes mask to <prefix>_INT_CLEAR and then to <prefix>_INT_MASK. It returns nothing.
note: item named panthor_<name>_irq_resume; generated at panthor_device.h:433-439. The round 15 reviewer claim about INT_STAT is not applicable to this function. R:n/a

name: PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER(__name, __reg_prefix, __handler)
prose: Static function generated by the PANTHOR_IRQ_HANDLER macro as panthor_request_<name>_irq(ptdev, pirq, irq, mask). It stores ptdev and irq in pirq, calls the generated resume function with mask (so the interrupt registers are programmed before the handlers are registered), and returns the result of devm_request_threaded_irq on ptdev->base.dev for that irq, with the generated raw and threaded handlers, IRQF_SHARED, the name KBUILD_MODNAME followed by - and the macro's name, and pirq as the cookie: 0 on success or the negative error from that call. A failed registration leaves the interrupt registers programmed by the resume call.

name: dce4_crtc_do_set_base
prose: Static int (atombios_crtc.c:1134-1453), the Evergreen/DCE4 scanout-base programming. With atomic == 0 and no framebuffer bound to the primary plane it returns 0 at once; the target framebuffer is fb when atomic is set and the primary plane's framebuffer otherwise. It reserves the buffer object (the reservation error is returned before any register is touched); in the atomic case it takes the current GPU offset, otherwise it pins the object in VRAM, and a pin failure unreserves and returns -EINVAL. It reads the tiling flags, unreserves, and chooses the surface format and endian swap from the framebuffer's pixel format (the 10-bit formats set bypass_lut); an unsupported format returns -EINVAL after the reservation was released, leaving a buffer pinned in the non-atomic case. It then derives the tiling, bank, pipe-config fields per ASIC family (on CIK a computed tile index of 16 or more logs and returns -EINVAL), programs the CRTC's graphics surface address, format, swap, pitch, viewport, desktop height and the LUT bypass bit, and, if not atomic and a different old framebuffer was passed, reserves it (a reservation failure returns that error) and unpins it. It finally calls radeon_bandwidth_update and returns 0.

The old prose omitted the early return 0 without a framebuffer, the CIK tile-index -EINVAL and the old-framebuffer unpin. R:n/a

name: atombios_crtc_program_ss
prose: Static void (atombios_crtc.c:443-550) with no return value. With enable nonzero it returns at once when ss->percentage is 0 or ss->type has ATOM_EXTERNAL_SS_MASK set; with enable zero it returns at once when another enabled CRTC (index different from crtc_id) uses the same pll_id. Otherwise it fills the ATOM argument structure by ASIC generation: DCE5 (v3, amount, step and type with the PLL selection bits; ATOM_PPLL_INVALID returns without executing), DCE4 (v2, same pll handling), DCE3 (v1 with percentage, type, step, delay, range, pll id and enable), AVIVO (it calls atombios_disable_ss and returns when enable is ATOM_DISABLE or the percentage is 0 or the type is external; since the early returns above already cover the enable case with percentage 0 or external SS, this condition effectively only happens for enable == ATOM_DISABLE), and older ASICs (for ATOM_DISABLE it calls atombios_disable_ss and returns). In every remaining case it executes the EnableSpreadSpectrumOnPPLL ATOM table with the argument block.

name: radeon_process_i2c_ch
prose: Static int (atombios_i2c.c:36-98). It takes chan->mutex and then the ATOM scratch mutex, and releases both before every return. For a write (HW_I2C_WRITE set in flags) it returns -EINVAL when num is above ATOM_MAX_HW_I2C_WRITE (3); otherwise it sets the register index from buf[0] (0 if buf is NULL), decrements num when it is nonzero and copies the remaining num bytes from buf[1] into a 16-bit output value (so num - 1 data bytes are sent for num of 1 or more, and 0 for num 0). For a read the register index and output are 0. It then fills the ATOM argument block (flags, speed, byte count, slave address shifted left by one, line number) and executes ProcessI2cChannelTransaction. If the returned status is not HW_ASSISTED_I2C_STATUS_SUCCESS it returns -EIO without modifying buf; otherwise, for a read it copies num bytes from the ATOM scratch area into buf with radeon_atom_copy_swap, and it returns 0.

name: evergreen_gpu_init
prose: Static void (evergreen.c:3132-3707); it has no return statement (and returns nothing). It switches on rdev->family to fill rdev->config.evergreen with per-ASIC values (num_ses, max_pipes, max_tile_pipes, max_simds, max_backends, max_gprs, max_threads, max_gs_threads, max_stack_entries, sx and sc sizes, max_hw_contexts, sq_num_cf_insts), computes tile_config from the pipe count, the IGP flag or the memory bank configuration and gb_addr_config, determines the disabled render backends (from fuse straps for CEDAR to HEMLOCK, otherwise per shader engine) and the active SIMDs from CC_GC_SHADER_PIPE_CONFIG, programs GB_ADDR_CONFIG and the other address-config registers, the backend map (stored in config.evergreen.backend_map), the CP, TA, SX, SMX, PA_SC, SPI, SQ resource-management and VGT registers (with per-family thread counts and cache invalidation mode), clears the color base, perf counter and constant-buffer registers, sets the HDP flush-invalidate bit, and ends with a 50 microsecond delay.

name: evergreen_packet3_check
prose: Static int (evergreen_cs.c:1773-2761) that validates one type-3 command packet in an Evergreen command stream; its body is a switch on pkt->opcode. For each supported opcode it checks the packet's count and field values, fetches relocation entries with radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc where an address is present, patches the IB words with the relocated GPU offset, updates the tracker, and for draw and dispatch packets calls evergreen_cs_track_check. It returns 0 when the packet passes (including SET_PREDICATION with a clear operation, which returns 0 early, and NOP). It returns -EINVAL for a wrong packet count, an invalid field, a buffer that is too small for the access, an unsupported opcode, and also when a required relocation cannot be obtained (radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc failures are converted to -EINVAL after a warning); only the result of evergreen_cs_track_check is returned unchanged, so those errors can be other negative values.

Reviewer claim (relocation failures return -EINVAL, not the error from radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc as the old prose said) is right (for example 1923-1927); evergreen_cs_track_check errors are returned as is (1908-1911). The function is long (about 990 lines and many return points), so this prose is deliberately general. R:right

name: evergreen_cs_parse
prose: Returns int (evergreen_cs.c:2763-2877) and parses a whole indirect buffer. If p->track is NULL it allocates a tracker with kzalloc (returning -ENOMEM on failure, with nothing to free), initialises it with evergreen_cs_track_init, picks the register safety bitmap and the tile configuration by family (Cayman or Evergreen), derives npipes, nbanks, group_size and row_size from the tile configuration and stores it in p->track; a tracker that is already present is used as it is. It then loops while p->idx is below the IB length: it parses the packet header with radeon_cs_packet_parse (an error frees the tracker, sets p->track to NULL and is returned), advances p->idx past the packet, and handles type 0 with evergreen_cs_parse_packet0, type 2 as a no-op and type 3 with evergreen_packet3_check; an unknown packet type frees the tracker and returns -EINVAL, and a nonzero result from the type 0 or type 3 handler frees the tracker and returns it. When the loop completes it frees the tracker, sets p->track to NULL and returns 0. The tracker is freed on every path after the allocation.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at evergreen_cs.c:2763). Reviewer claim (the old prose omitted track init and packet2 and wrongly required a preinitialised tracker) is partly right: a NULL tracker is allocated here (2770-2775); evergreen_cs_track_init has no return value and type 2 packets only advance the index. R:mixed

name: evergreen_dma_cs_parse
prose: Returns int (evergreen_cs.c:2888-3314) and validates and relocates a whole DMA indirect buffer, looping over its packets. At the start of each iteration it returns -EINVAL if p->idx is not below the chunk length. It decodes the DMA command, count and sub-command from the header word and switches on the command: WRITE (needs a destination relocation through r600_dma_cs_next_reloc; sub-commands 0 and 8 patch the offset words, advance p->idx by count plus 3 or 7, and then check that the written range fits the destination object), COPY (needs source and destination relocations; the sub-commands handle linear, tiled and partial copy forms, check that the source and destination ranges fit their objects, patch the offsets and advance p->idx by the packet size), CONSTANT_FILL (destination relocation, patched offset words, size check, advance by 4) and NOP (advance by 1). It returns -EINVAL for a missing relocation, an unsupported command or sub-command, or a range that exceeds a buffer object; in the WRITE case p->idx and the patched IB words have already been advanced before the size check, so p->idx is not left at the offending packet. When the loop ends it returns 0.

The old prose described a single-packet parser and claimed p->idx is not advanced on error, which is wrong for the WRITE case. R:n/a

name: kv_parse_sys_info_table

If the table's content revision is not 8 it logs and returns -EINVAL without changing pi. Otherwise it fills pi->sys_info with the boot-up engine and UMA clocks and NB voltage index, htc_tmp_lmt (203 when the BIOS byte is 0) and htc_hyst_lmt (5 when 0) (logging an error, but continuing, when the first is not above the second), nb_dpm_enable from bit 3 of ulSystemConfig, and the KV_NUM_NBPSTATES NB p-state memory and n clocks; it sets pi->caps_enable_dfs_bypass to true when the DFS-bypass bit of ulGPUCapInfo is set (otherwise leaving it unchanged), builds the sclk voltage mapping table and vid mapping table with sumo_construct_sclk_voltage_mapping_table and sumo_construct_vid_mapping_table, fills rdev->pm.dpm.dyn_state.max_clock_voltage_on_ac with kv_construct_max_power_limits_table and returns 0.

name: r100_pm_get_dynpm_state
prose: Void function (r100.c:224-304). It first sets dynpm_can_upclock and dynpm_can_downclock to true. By dynpm_planned_action: MINIMUM sets requested_power_state_index to 0 and clears can_downclock; DOWNCLOCK at current index 0 keeps the index and clears can_downclock, otherwise with more than one active CRTC it scans from index 0 for the first state without RADEON_PM_STATE_SINGLE_DISPLAY_ONLY and requests the current index if that state's index is at or above it and that state's index otherwise (leaving the request unchanged if every state has the flag), and with at most one active CRTC it requests current - 1; afterwards, if any CRTC is active and the requested state's first clock info has RADEON_PM_MODE_NO_DISPLAY, the request is incremented. UPCLOCK at the last state keeps the index and clears can_upclock; otherwise with more than one active CRTC it scans from the top for the first state without the single-display flag and requests the current index if that state's index is at or below it and that state's index otherwise, and with fewer CRTCs it requests current + 1. DEFAULT requests the default state index and clears can_upclock. DYNPM_ACTION_NONE or any other value logs an error and returns at once, leaving requested_power_state_index and requested_clock_mode_index unchanged. In the other cases it sets requested_clock_mode_index to 0 and emits a driver debug message with the requested clocks.

Reviewer claims: NONE/default returns early without setting requested_clock_mode_index (right, 289-292), multi-CRTC cases pick the lowest/highest usable state (right, 240-251 and 268-279), only DRM_ERROR on the early return and a DRM_DEBUG_DRIVER message otherwise (right, 291 and 297). name: r100_packet0_check
prose: Static int (r100.c:1585-1924) that validates one register write of a type-0 packet and updates the command-stream tracker; the body is a switch on reg. Per register it records tracked state (texture parameters, colour buffer pitch and cpp, depth buffer pitch, maxy, vertex size, vap_vf_cntl, dirty flags) from the IB value, and for registers holding an address it gets a relocation with radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc and patches ib[idx]: for RB3D_COLOROFFSET and similar address registers it adds the relocation's GPU offset, but for RB3D_COLORPITCH it only uses the relocation's tiling flags to rewrite the tiling bits of the pitch word (when RADEON_CS_KEEP_TILING_FLAGS is clear; otherwise the value is kept) and does not add the GPU offset. It returns 0 when the register is handled, returns the error of r100_cs_packet_parse_vline, r100_reloc_pitch_offset or radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc unchanged, and returns -EINVAL for an invalid RB3D colour format or a register that is not handled.

name: r100_cs_track_check
prose: Returns int (r100.c:2272-2407) and checks the tracked state before a draw. It sets num_cb to track->num_cb only when cb_dirty is set (and to 0 when no colour write can happen: no clear, empty colour channel mask and no blend read). For each colour buffer it returns -EINVAL if the buffer object is NULL or pitch * cpp * maxy plus the offset exceeds the object size; then it clears cb_dirty (so an early return leaves it set). If zb_dirty and z_enabled are set it does the same size check for the depth buffer, then clears zb_dirty; if aa_dirty and aaresolve are set it checks the AA buffer and clears aa_dirty. It then decodes the primitive walk from vap_vf_cntl: walk 1 and 2 check each vertex array for a bound object and its size (-EINVAL), walk 3 checks that vtx_size * nverts equals immd_dwords (-EINVAL), and any other walk returns -EINVAL. Finally, if tex_dirty is set it clears it first and returns the result of r100_cs_track_texture_check (which can return -EINVAL or the -1 from r100_cs_track_cube); otherwise it returns 0. Hence the dirty flags of checks that already completed are cleared even if a later check fails.
note: Checked against r100.c:2272-2407. Reviewer claims: dirty flags are cleared before later checks can fail (right), the texture check can return -1 via r100_cs_track_cube and tex_dirty is cleared even when it fails (right, 2402-2404), and it can also return -EINVAL (right, it returns whatever r100_cs_track_texture_check returns). name: r100_bandwidth_update
prose: Void function (r100.c:3171-3673). It returns at once if rdev->mode_info.mode_config_initialized is false. Otherwise it updates the display priority, takes the mode and framebuffer pixel size of CRTC 0 when it is enabled and, unless the device is a single-CRTC part, of CRTC 1 when enabled. It then evaluates the memory and display timing model with fixed-point arithmetic (memory timings read from MEM_CNTL, MEM_SDRAM_MODE_REG and MEM_TIMING_CNTL, peak display bandwidth against memory bandwidth with a DRM_ERROR warning when the bandwidth may be insufficient) and programs the display buffer control registers (GRPH_BUFFER_CNTL and GRPH2_BUFFER_CNTL, and on RS400/RS480 the fixed DISP/DMIF request registers) for each enabled CRTC. At the end it sets lb_vblank_lead_lines of each enabled CRTC to the line buffer size divided (rounded up) by its horizontal display size. It returns nothing.

name: r300_packet0_check
prose: Static int (r300.c:627-1171) that validates one register write of a type-0 packet and updates the command-stream tracker; the body is a switch on reg. It returns 0 when the register is handled; it returns the error of r100_cs_packet_parse_vline, r100_reloc_pitch_offset or radeon_cs_packet_next_reloc unchanged; and it returns -EINVAL (through the fail label, after logging the register) for an invalid texture or colour format, a forbidden value or an unknown register.
